### Meek like Moses
Author: Rebecca VanDoodewaard
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/meek-like-moses
Passage: Numbers 12:3
Points:
- True biblical meekness is strength under control, not timid weakness or a lack of conviction.
- Like Moses, the meek are gentle regarding personal grievances but courageous and bold for God’s honor.
- Surrendering our desires to God brings an inward composure that silences anxiety and emotional turmoil.
- Practicing selfless humility equips believers to endure hard providences and serve the kingdom sacrificially.
- Moses pointed forward to Jesus Christ, who embodied perfect meekness in submitting fully to the Father’s will.

### Meekness and Self-Control
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/meekness-and-self-control
Passage: Numbers 12:3
Points:
- Meekness is often mistaken for weakness, yet Moses demonstrated immense strength and tested leadership.
- Biblical gentleness stems from quiet confidence and security in God rather than arrogance or intimidation.
- A meek spirit produces self-restraint and prevents believers from reacting with violence or indulgence.
- Cultivating the fruit of the Spirit creates stability and trustworthiness, preparing Christians for godly leadership.

### Bible Pathway - Feb. 18, 2010
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-feb-18-2010-11626381.html
Passage: Numbers 12:1-3
Points:
- Spiritual gifts and privileges can easily foster pride and competitive jealousy when others receive recognition.
- Miriam hid her envy and resentment behind spiritual sounding criticisms, but the Lord saw her true heart.
- God directly defended His servant Moses and demonstrated severe displeasure against rebellion by striking Miriam with leprosy.
- Believers must guard against pride and follow the humble, meek example modeled by Moses and fulfilled in Christ.

### Devotional: Numbers 12-13
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numbers-12-13-psalm-49-isaiah-2-hebrews-10/
Passage: Numbers 12:1-16
Points:
- Sinful rebellion among believers often masks selfish ambition and envy behind seemingly sensible, democratic objections.
- Moses’ exceptional humility kept him from self-defensive turf protection when his leadership was attacked.
- God personally stepped in to affirm Moses' unique status as a faithful servant who received direct revelation.
- Miriam’s chastisement and temporary exclusion from camp underscored that grasping for power invites divine judgment.
